info.short_description: Child's age in years, limited to the measure's own age range (named in the measure, e.g. _3_17). Each measure has a row for its full range (e.g. '3-17'; '0-17' for measures with no age suffix) plus the bands 0-5, 6-11 and 12-17 cut to that range (e.g. '3-5'). '6mo-5' means 6 months to 5 years. A measure that fits inside one band (e.g. _12_17) has only that band.
Which NSCH measure the row reports. Each value is defined in the table of values below.
Weighted percent of children in the measure's age range, for this state, year and group. NA when suppressed.
Lower bound of the 95% confidence interval for value, from the survey design, on the logit scale. NA when value is NA, 0 or 100.
Upper bound of the 95% confidence interval for value, from the survey design, on the logit scale. NA when value is NA, 0 or 100.
Unweighted number of surveyed children in the denominator of value.
1 if fewer than 30 children were surveyed, so value and its interval are NA (not imputed); 0 otherwise. Ages and years a measure does not cover have no row.
1 if the 95% confidence interval is wider than 20 percentage points or 1.2 times the estimate, or the estimate is 0 or 100; NA when suppressed; 0 otherwise.

nsch_pct_flourishing_6_17.short_description: Percent of children ages 6-17 whose parent says they always or usually show curiosity about learning, finish tasks they start, and stay calm when challenged (all three).
nsch_pct_flourishing_6_17.long_description: Percent of children ages 6-17 whose parent says they always or usually show curiosity about learning, finish tasks they start, and stay calm when challenged (all three). From the National Survey of Children's Health (NSCH); all answers are reported by a parent or caregiver. Definition: A child counts as flourishing only if the parent answered 'Always' or 'Usually' to all three questions; a skipped question counts as not met. Children with all three questions skipped are excluded. Reported for data years 2018 onward. It matches the 'Meets all 3 flourishing items' category of indicator 2.4 from the Data Resource Center for Child and Adolescent Health (childhealthdata.org). The row whose age is the full range covers all children ages 6-17; age bands are cut to that range.
nsch_pct_flourishing_6_17.statement: In {location}, {value} of children ages 6-17 whose parent says they always or usually show curiosity about learning, finish tasks they start, and stay calm when challenged (all three).

nsch_pct_flourishing_6mo_5.short_description: Percent of children ages 6 months-5 years whose parent says they are always or usually affectionate, curious, smiling and laughing, and quick to bounce back (all four).
nsch_pct_flourishing_6mo_5.long_description: Percent of children ages 6 months-5 years whose parent says they are always or usually affectionate, curious, smiling and laughing, and quick to bounce back (all four). From the National Survey of Children's Health (NSCH); all answers are reported by a parent or caregiver. Definition: A child counts as flourishing only if the parent answered 'Always' or 'Usually' to all four questions; a skipped question counts as not met. Children younger than 6 months and children with all four questions skipped are excluded. Reported for data years 2018 onward. It matches the 'Meets all 4 flourishing items' category of indicator 2.3 from the Data Resource Center for Child and Adolescent Health (childhealthdata.org). The row whose age is the full range covers all children ages 6 months-5 years; age bands are cut to that range.
nsch_pct_flourishing_6mo_5.statement: In {location}, {value} of children ages 6 months-5 years whose parent says they are always or usually affectionate, curious, smiling and laughing, and quick to bounce back (all four).

nsch_pct_depression_anxiety_12_17.long_name: NSCH: Current depression or anxiety, ages 12-17
nsch_pct_depression_anxiety_12_17.short_description: Percent of adolescents ages 12-17 whose parent reports they currently have depression or anxiety problems diagnosed by a health care provider.
nsch_pct_depression_anxiety_12_17.long_description: Percent of adolescents ages 12-17 whose parent reports they currently have depression or anxiety problems diagnosed by a health care provider. From the National Survey of Children's Health (NSCH); all answers are reported by a parent or caregiver. Definition: An adolescent counts if a health care provider ever said they had depression or anxiety problems and the parent says they currently have it. Adolescents never diagnosed count as not having either condition. Reported for data years 2016 onward. The row whose age is the full range covers all adolescents ages 12-17; age bands are cut to that range.
nsch_pct_depression_anxiety_12_17.statement: In {location}, {value} of adolescents ages 12-17 whose parent reports they currently have depression or anxiety problems diagnosed by a health care provider.

Definition: Includes only adolescents who needed to see a mental health professional in the past 12 months; an adolescent counts if they received treatment or counseling. nsch_pct_adult_mentor_12_17.statement: In {location}, {value} of adolescents ages 12-17 with at least one adult outside the home whom they can rely on for advice or guidance.

nsch_pct_aces_2plus.short_name: Two or more adverse childhood experiences
nsch_pct_aces_2plus.long_name: NSCH: Two or more adverse childhood experiences
nsch_pct_aces_2plus.short_description: Percent of children ages 0-17 who have had two or more adverse childhood experiences, such as parental divorce, a parent in jail, or witnessing violence.
nsch_pct_aces_2plus.long_description: Percent of children ages 0-17 who have had two or more adverse childhood experiences, such as parental divorce, a parent in jail, or witnessing violence. From the National Survey of Children's Health (NSCH); all answers are reported by a parent or caregiver. Definition: Experiences counted: hard to cover basics like food or housing on the family's income, parent divorced or separated, parent died, parent served time in jail or prison, violence between adults in the home, victim or witness of neighborhood violence, lived with someone mentally ill or with an alcohol or drug problem, and treated unfairly because of race or ethnicity or a health condition. A child counts with two or more; children with every question skipped are excluded. Reported for data years 2016 onward. Unfair treatment because of a health condition or disability was added in 2021, so 2016-2020 counts are out of nine experiences instead of ten. The row whose age is the full range covers all children ages 0-17; age bands are cut to that range.
nsch_pct_aces_2plus.statement: In {location}, {value} of children ages 0-17 who have had two or more adverse childhood experiences, such as parental divorce, a parent in jail, or witnessing violence.

nsch_pct_health_excellent_vgood.long_description: Percent of children ages 0-17 whose parent rates their health as excellent or very good. From the National Survey of Children's Health (NSCH); all answers are reported by a parent or caregiver. The row whose age is the full range covers all children ages 0-17; age bands are cut to that range.
nsch_pct_health_excellent_vgood.statement: In {location}, {value} of children ages 0-17 whose parent rates their health as excellent or very good.

nsch_pct_obesity_6_17.long_description: Percent of children ages 6-17 with obesity (body mass index at or above the 95th percentile). From the National Survey of Children's Health (NSCH); all answers are reported by a parent or caregiver. Definition: A child counts if their body mass index is at or above the 95th percentile. nsch_pct_obesity_6_17.statement: In {location}, {value} of children ages 6-17 with obesity (body mass index at or above the 95th percentile).

nsch_pct_active_daily_6_11.statement: In {location}, {value} of children ages 6-11 who were physically active for at least 60 minutes every day in the past week.

nsch_pct_well_visit_12_17.short_description: Percent of adolescents ages 12-17 with at least one preventive medical check-up in the past year.
nsch_pct_well_visit_12_17.long_description: Percent of adolescents ages 12-17 with at least one preventive medical check-up in the past year. From the National Survey of Children's Health (NSCH); all answers are reported by a parent or caregiver. Definition: An adolescent counts if they had one or more preventive check-ups in the past 12 months. Adolescents with no health care visit of any kind count as not having one. Reported for data years 2016-2017 and 2019 onward (not reported for 2018). Telehealth visits are included from 2021. The row whose age is the full range covers all adolescents ages 12-17; age bands are cut to that range.
nsch_pct_well_visit_12_17.statement: In {location}, {value} of adolescents ages 12-17 with at least one preventive medical check-up in the past year.

Children with no dental care of any kind count as not having one. Reported for data years 2016 onward. The row whose age is the full range covers all children ages 1-17; age bands are cut to that range.
nsch_pct_preventive_dental_1_17.statement: In {location}, {value} of children ages 1-17 with at least one preventive dental visit in the past year.

nsch_pct_tooth_decay_1_17.statement: In {location}, {value} of children ages 1-17 who had frequent or chronic decayed teeth or cavities in the past year.

nsch_pct_adequately_insured.short_description: Percent of children ages 0-17 who were insured all year with adequate coverage (meets their needs, lets them see needed providers, and has reasonable costs).
nsch_pct_adequately_insured.long_description: Percent of children ages 0-17 who were insured all year with adequate coverage (meets their needs, lets them see needed providers, and has reasonable costs). nsch_pct_forgone_care.statement: In {location}, {value} of children ages 0-17 who needed health care in the past year but did not receive it.

nsch_pct_food_sufficient_0_11.short_description: Percent of children ages 0-11 whose household could always afford to eat good, nutritious meals in the past year.
nsch_pct_food_sufficient_0_11.long_description: Percent of children ages 0-11 whose household could always afford to eat good, nutritious meals in the past year. From the National Survey of Children's Health (NSCH); all answers are reported by a parent or caregiver. Definition: A child counts if the household could always afford good, nutritious meals; the rest had enough to eat but not always the right kinds of food, or sometimes or often could not afford enough. Higher values are better. Reported for data years 2016 onward. The row whose age is the full range covers all children ages 0-11; age bands are cut to that range.
nsch_pct_food_sufficient_0_11.statement: In {location}, {value} of children ages 0-11 whose household could always afford to eat good, nutritious meals in the past year.

nsch_pct_housing_instability_0_11.short_name: Housing instability in past year, ages 0-11
nsch_pct_housing_instability_0_11.long_name: NSCH: Housing instability in past year, ages 0-11
nsch_pct_housing_instability_0_11.short_description: Percent of children ages 0-11 who experienced housing instability: ever homeless, a late rent or mortgage payment in the past year, or two or more moves in the past year.
nsch_pct_housing_instability_0_11.long_description: Percent of children ages 0-11 who experienced housing instability: ever homeless, a late rent or mortgage payment in the past year, or two or more moves in the past year. From the National Survey of Children's Health (NSCH); all answers are reported by a parent or caregiver. Definition: A child counts if they were ever homeless or lived in a shelter, the family could not pay the rent or mortgage on time in the past 12 months, or the child moved two or more times in the past 12 months. 'Don't know' and skipped questions do not count as instability. Reported for data years 2022 onward. The moves question changed format in 2024. The row whose age is the full range covers all children ages 0-11; age bands are cut to that range.
nsch_pct_housing_instability_0_11.statement: In {location}, {value} of children ages 0-11 who experienced housing instability: ever homeless, a late rent or mortgage payment in the past year, or two or more moves in the past year.

nsch_pct_household_smoking.long_description: Percent of children ages 0-17 who live with someone who uses cigarettes, cigars, or pipe tobacco. nsch.name: National Survey of Children's Health (NSCH)
nsch.organization: Health Resources and Services Administration, Maternal and Child Health Bureau (HRSA MCHB); conducted by the U.S. Census Bureau
nsch.location: NSCH public-use topical data files (Stata), 2016 onward, and the Title V measure code (SAS, 2016-2025)
nsch.description: The NSCH is an annual, cross-sectional, address-based household survey that produces national and state-level data on the physical and emotional health of children ages 0-17 in the United States. A parent or caregiver familiar with the child's health answers by web or mailed paper questionnaire about one randomly selected child in the household. It is sponsored by HRSA's Maternal and Child Health Bureau and conducted by the U.S. Census Bureau, and was redesigned in 2016; the Census Bureau advises that estimates from 2016 onward should not be compared with earlier NSCH surveys. Survey weights represent the non-institutionalized population of children residing in housing units in each state and DC. PopHIVE computes the estimates here from the public-use topical microdata: measures are coded with the Title V measure code that the Census Bureau publishes with the data files (or, for the few measures marked as NSCH survey items, as a single response category of one question), and are weighted single-year percentages with 95% logit confidence intervals that account for the survey design. Following the NSCH Comprehensive Analytic Guide, estimates with an unweighted denominator under 30 are suppressed and estimates whose 95% CI is wider than 20 percentage points or 1.2 times the estimate are flagged as unreliable. Single-year state estimates for small subgroups (for example, some race/ethnicity groups) are often suppressed or unreliable; the Census Bureau notes that multiple years can be combined for more precision. All responses are parent/caregiver reported. Time is the survey (data) year, coded YYYY-12-31; data collection for a survey year can extend into the following calendar year.
nsch.restrictions: Public use data. Per the Census Bureau NSCH FAQ: 'Data users are free to produce and publish works based on the NSCH data and documentation; proper attribution to the NSCH source material should accompany these works.' Suggested citation: Health Resources and Services Administration, Maternal and Child Health Bureau. [Year] National Survey of Children's Health Public Use Microdata File, STATA. Administered by the U.S. Census Bureau.
